We are already using Vite so I think this makes sense. Also Vue 3 and Vitest go well together. 

Jest is a bigger ecosystem right and been around longer?

https://github.com/jestjs/jest 45.5k stars 
https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest 15.7k stars

Yes, since vitest is built-in to Vite, there is no duplicate configuration or separate babel/webpack setup.  Plus Vite has a Jest-Compatible API, which you can see in many spots in this patch.  It also has first-class TypeScript support, which will become important once we land codegen from Redfish API (and that PR is UP!)

You could add a bit more to the commit msg if you want. You could also link a site or two that compares them. I think this is a no-brainer since we are using Vite, vitest is faster, near zero config and modern. The bigger ecosystem / more plugins argument for Jest seems to also hold less weight as the vitest ecosystem has continued to grow.
Done
where are you using this happy-dom ?

happy-dom is an alternative to jsdom.
It is used with the Vitest test runner for high speed unit tests.
Acknowledged

Done.

There are only 3 SVG imports in the codebase, stubbing them removed ~60 lines of path data for each, making the snapshots easier to read and compare.  All other SVGs, like the Carbon icons, still show their paths but are small.

vue3-snapshot-serializer was brought in to remove the data-v-* attributes (also sorts and normalizes class names alphabetically)
Done

Why `globals: true` ?

but still 
`import { vi, describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';`

`globals: false` ?
@gunnar@gmills.xyz I don't see this.  Can you elaborate?
I had it set to false, but ran into too many issues with the vue-i18n lib, especially when using with the unit tests (each test would have to load all language files IIRC).

My commit message here explains it: https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/webui-vue/+/86494/4//COMMIT_MSG#7

We have to keep i18n global as long as as we are using in with the old Options API.
I vote that we keep the import with goal of removing globals once we get rid of the options API (that is quite a few components to port to the Composition API!)

I think the document for unit testing also needs to be updated which is present under /docs/guide/unit-testing
It still mentions jest

Done.

Updated the Unit Test guide and added some examples.

Note: there are many other doc updates needed given all the recent vue2 -> vue3 migration changes

Yeah we should raise a seperate Patch for them as well
Its not good to keep them outdated
We should do it when most of the changes for vue3 is done (Like pinia,vite ,composition API etc)
Do you have any other thoughts?
+1, We should update the docs. (Vitepress)

+1, Yes, we should do a Docs update (agree on Vitepress) and migration sometime after this patchset is merged.  This will also allow us to clean up a lot of the npm install noise related to vuepress!

I think that the store and composition API migration will take a long time, and we should not block doc updates on them.  Those related docs can be updated along with those tasks.

As discussed over discord ,Jason whats your take on the docs for this PR?
Are you going to put it here alongside or will have them in a separate PR with vitepress?

Anyways I am good with this PR as it is
We can carry the vitepress discussion elsewhere and not hold 
this PR because of it
Done

OK, that was painful!

Two issues addressed here while dealing with build failures due to doc updates:
1. The project had no local prettier configuration matching CI's settings
2. the pre-commit hooks were broken (yorkie was removed during Vite migration but lint-staged remained orphaned).

Fix: Added .prettierrc.yaml matching CI configuration, installed simple-git-hooks to restore working pre-commit hooks, and formatted all affected files.
Acknowledged
